errors.text: Misidentifies the targeted property as stacking-fault energy and mechanical/phase stability; the hidden target is improvement of magnetic coercivity beyond the approximately 100 Oe limit of single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloys.
Replaces the FeCoNiTi fcc–C14 dual-phase intervention with computational inclusion of longitudinal spin fluctuations.

Conflates spin moments induced by longitudinal spin fluctuations with orbital magnetic moments. The cited evidence concerns finite spin/local moments in CoCrFeMnNi and does not establish the target orbital-moment contribution to coercivity.
Omits the central dual-phase mechanism: coupling of ferromagnetic fcc and C14 Laves phases, spin-canted components, and domain-wall pinning.
Fails to reconstruct the key outcome of approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K and the distinct magnetic transitions at 1084, 214, and 168 K.
Uses evidence from the Cantor alloy's fcc–hcp thermodynamics to make claims about Fe-Co-Ni-derived coercivity without adequate transfer justification.
